| **Weight, in kg ($y$)** | $30$ | $34$ | $38$ | $42$ |

Tara plays soccer. The table above shows the ages and corresponding weights of four of Tara's teammates.
Compute the covariance of the data sets given that the means are $\overset{―}{x}=12$ and $\overset{―}{y}=36.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(10\,-\,12)(30\,-\,36)+(11\,-\,12)(34\,-\,36)+(12\,-\,12)(38\,-\,36)+(15\,-\,12)(42\,-\,36)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-2)(-6)+(-1)(-2)+(0)(2)+(3)(6)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[12+2+0+18] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 32 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
